The Journal
Notes · 2026

A subdivision begins as one shape

A subdivision begins as one shape.

Then the questions start cutting into it.

Road
Does every lot have legal, usable access?
Frontage
Does each lot meet the frontage it needs?
Topography
Where can a road actually go?
Water
How is each lot served?
Sewer or septic
What density does that allow?
Drainage
Where does the water go?
Soil
What can the ground actually support?
Regulation
What does the county permit?
Market
What lot, and what home, is actually moving?
Cost
What does the infrastructure do to the basis?
Exit
Who ultimately buys the lots?

Every answer takes something away from the original shape.

The acreage never survives intact.

What remains is the project.

This is how I approach the problem. It is not a rule for anyone else’s land.
